protocol.assurance: Each repair agent was instructed to read only its sanitized fixture. Native subagents share a filesystem, so this is an instruction-based boundary rather than proof of filesystem isolation.

verifier_boundary.purpose: Validate candidate changes and hidden differential behavior; verifier access does not imply repair-agent access.

fixture_construction.method: git archive of the pinned revision containing only the allowed fixture paths
fixture_construction.initial_issue: The first minimal archive omitted conftest.py, causing pytest collection to fail because pytest.use_correct was undefined.
fixture_construction.resolution: The original conftest.py was added before either repair was evaluated; both fixtures then reproduced the same three public failures.

limitations: QuixBugs explicitly contains small injected defects, so this case is a repair-discipline and regression check rather than a realistic distributed-systems causality benchmark.
The result compares two single runs from the same agent platform and cannot estimate a model-wide causal effect of the Skill.

The reference implementation has an undocumented precondition: a fully disconnected one-way edge can raise KeyError. Hidden checks therefore use only inputs that the reference implementation itself accepts.

Defects4J, Bugs.jar, BugsInPy, Codeflaws, and BugSwarm were investigated but were not scored because their required toolchains, artifacts, architecture, or dependencies were unavailable in this environment.
